text: That very singular man, old Doctor Heidegger, once invited four venerable friends to meet him in his study, where he intended to conduct a peculiar experiment. <break time="0.8s" /> There were three white bearded gentlemen, Mister Medbourne, Colonel Killigrew, and Mister Gascoigne, and a withered lady whose name was the Widow Wycherly. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Medbourne, in the vigor of his age, had been a prosperous merchant, but he had lost everything through a frantic speculation and was now little better than a beggar. <break time="0.8s" /> Colonel Killigrew had wasted his best years, his health, and his fortune in the pursuit of sinful pleasures, which had left him with a body tormented by gout. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Gascoigne was a ruined politician, a man of evil fame, who had been so completely forgotten that the present generation scarcely knew his name. <break time="0.8s" /> As for the Widow Wycherly, she had been a great beauty in her day, but scandalous stories had driven her from society, and she now lived in deep seclusion. <break time="0.8s" /> It is worth mentioning that each of the three old gentlemen had once been on the point of cutting the others throats for her sake. <break time="0.8s" /> Before going further, we must also say that Doctor Heidegger and all his guests were commonly thought to be a little out of their minds.
